prompt: A motion graph has a horizontal section where the value on the vertical axis is non-zero. Which row correctly identifies the state of motion for each graph type?
options: displacement-time: moving with constant velocity; velocity-time: stationary
displacement-time: stationary; velocity-time: moving with constant velocity
displacement-time: accelerating uniformly; velocity-time: moving with constant velocity

answer.explanation: On a displacement-time graph, a horizontal line means displacement is constant, so gradient = 0 and the object is stationary. On a velocity-time graph, a non-zero horizontal line means velocity is constant, so the object moves with constant velocity.

distractor_explanations: Reverses both interpretations: displacement constant means stationary, not constant velocity.
Correct: displacement-time horizontal means stationary; velocity-time horizontal means constant velocity.
A horizontal line on a velocity-time graph has zero gradient, so acceleration is zero, not uniform non-zero acceleration.
A horizontal line on a displacement-time graph indicates zero velocity, not acceleration.
hints: What does a horizontal line mean for the rate of change of the vertical quantity?
If displacement is unchanging, is the object moving?
solution: B. Displacement-time: stationary (v = 0). Velocity-time: moving with constant velocity (a = 0).
teacher_walkthrough: A horizontal section has gradient = 0 in both graphs.
For displacement-time: gradient = velocity = 0, so the object is stationary.
For velocity-time: gradient = acceleration = 0, while velocity is non-zero, so it moves with constant velocity.
